summary: Both hypotheses confirmed. The main arm (simulated annealing with precomputed per-edge expansion bounds) scored 89.53, well above the 85 target. The negative control (greedy-only, no SA) scored 20.25, confirming SA is the dominant scoring mechanism. The experiment is valid and the current best solution achieves strong partial credit on the judge.
key_points: h-main scored 89.53 (predicted >85) — CONFIRMED. The key algorithmic insight was precomputing max-expansion bounds per rectangle edge, making every SA proposal valid by construction and dramatically improving acceptance rates.

h-control-negative scored 20.25 (predicted 15–30) — CONFIRMED. Greedy expansion alone without SA optimization is insufficient, confirming that iterative stochastic optimization is the dominant contributor (~70 points of the score).

An unexpected finding: coordinated neighbor moves (adjusting adjacent rectangles together) were dropped because the O(N) adjacency search per SA step reduced total iteration count and actually hurt performance. Single-rectangle moves with bounded proposals were more effective.

Potential next steps to push beyond 89.5: try more sophisticated neighborhood structures (e.g., swap-based moves between adjacent companies), better initial placement via Voronoi partitioning, or tuning the SA cooling schedule and time allocation.
